propositions: A deterministic shadow comparator must consume the same call/result set as legacy and RP-06 projections, report field-level mismatches, emit no provider calls, and accept only an approved delta allowlist (built-in retune/disable, project DET inclusion, project LLM applicability, code-review budget enforcement, typed partial-failure continuation, success-only checkpointing).

Repository-policy guards must fail when review gates bypass CriteriaSnapshot for direct routing reads, when a second discovery scheduler is introduced outside the shared kernel, or when per-unit trace fields enter review/review-status schemas.

The live canary at tests/external/test_review_discovery_live.py must drive the real default discovery path through the external LLM provider matrix, prove at least one discovery call reaches each configured provider, assert the narrow final verdict (PASS/BLOCK), and verify the reducer-ignored internal journal is retained without printing secrets or raw trace.

New code must ignore legacy checkpoint envelopes, the retained compatibility projection must not write new envelopes or decide verdicts, and rollback requires only a code revert to the retained projection with no journal rewrite.

docs/review-kernel.md must document final ownership (gates own authored topology and strategy; snapshot and execution facts are shared; RP-01 owns provider-turn retry), approved deltas, sensitive-data boundary, shadow behavior, and revert-based rollback.

The external provider matrix canary executed on all three arms (anthropic, openai, bedrock) with >=1 real discovery call per arm reaching the configured provider (coverage.llm_ran=True), narrow verdicts returned (schema-conformant), and internal journals retained (sidecar_emitted=True).
